## Parent

Part of #23. Found while prototyping convenience API additions against the
tree at `bd0b3b3`, outside the scope of the final readiness review (#40).

## Status

**Reviewed and corrected; ready to merge.** Branch
`sayuks/verb-argument-admission`, rebased onto `main` (`406f132`) and now at
`1f02b32`. `/code-review` against `origin/main` ran with this issue as the Spec
input; its findings are resolved in the second commit and recorded under
*Review* below. Not `ready-for-agent` work — the code exists.

## Problem

Two admission gaps, both of which turn a caller's mistake into something other
than a clear error.

### A misspelled or removed option becomes a summary column

`summarize_with_margins()` collects summaries from `...`, so any named
expression is accepted. An argument name the verb does not have is therefore
not a mistake but a constant column. Against `bd0b3b3`:

```r
summarize_with_margins(
  data.frame(g = c("a", "a", "b"), v = c(1, 2, 3)),
  s = sum(v), .grouping = rollup(g), .sort = TRUE
)
#>       g s .sort
#> 1     a 3  TRUE
#> 2     b 3  TRUE
#> 3 Total 6  TRUE
```

`.sort` was removed in #15 (`94fad76`); a caller who read older material gets a
`.sort` column of `TRUE` instead of being told so. The near-miss spellings
behave no better: `.groupings = rollup(g)` errors only by accident, with

```
`.groupings` must be a vector, not a <margin_grouping_spec> object.
```

which never names `.grouping`, and `.margin_labels`, `.duplicate`, and `.ids`
each silently become columns.

### Input dplyr cannot group reports an internal generic

`normalize_grouping_input()` reaches `dplyr::group_vars()` before anything
validates the input. Against `bd0b3b3`:

```r
summarize_with_margins(as.matrix(data), s = sum(v), .grouping = rollup(g))
#> Error: no applicable method for 'group_vars' applied to an object of
#>   class "c('matrix', 'array', 'character')"
```

`NULL` gives the same shape. Both are `simpleError`, so a caller following
#23's user story 26 — handling package errors by class rather than by English
message text — catches nothing, and the message names a generic the caller
never called.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `check_option_named_summaries()` in `R/summary-selections.R` rejects a
      summary name that exactly matches a current option, or that is within
      `utils::adist() <= 1` of one, and names the option it resembles.
- [x] `removed_summary_options` records `.sort` separately, with a message
      that states the current contract — row order is unspecified — and points
      at `dplyr::arrange()` plus a `grouping_bit()` summary per dimension.
- [x] The check survives `!!!` splicing of an options list.
- [x] Ordinary leading-dot output names (`.n`, `.total_by_region`) and a
      genuine `.id = ".set"` are unaffected.
- [x] `assert_margin_input()` in `R/utils.R` duck-types the input by looking
      for a `dplyr::group_vars()` method and, when none dispatches, aborts with
      `marginplyr_error` naming the caller's argument. It is duck-typed rather
      than a class whitelist so that a backend dplyr supports is not rejected.
      Review changed *trying* to *looking for a method*: calling the generic
      and catching every error would report a backend's own failure as the
      caller having supplied the wrong kind of object.
- [x] Every entry point admits input the same way: `summarize_with_margins()`,
      `expand_with_margins()`, `nest_with_margins()`, `nest_by_with_margins()`,
      and `inspect_grouping()`.
- [x] `tests/testthat/test-verb-argument-admission.R` covers both halves and
      asserts that tibble, grouped data frames, dtplyr, and arrow input are
      still admitted. 23 expectations, all passing on the branch.
- [x] Rebase `sayuks/verb-argument-admission` onto `main`. Rebased onto
      `406f132` with no conflicts.
- [x] `/code-review` against `origin/main` with this issue as the Spec input;
      findings resolved. See *Review* below.
- [x] `pkgload::load_all(".", quiet = TRUE); lintr::lint_package()` is clean,
      and the full test suite passes: 1633 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips.
- [x] Decide and record whether the misspelling threshold stays at edit
      distance 1. **It stays at 1.** See *Misspelling threshold* below.

## Review

`/code-review` against `origin/main`, this issue as the Spec input. Four
findings, all resolved in `1f02b32`.

**The admission check sat in the shared module.** ADR 0001 leaves input-class
admission with each verb — every existing check honours that
(`assert_lazy_table()` in three verbs, `assert_nest_possible()` in the nesting
pipeline) — and `assert_margin_input()` had gone into
`normalize_grouping_input()`. Each verb now calls it beside the check it
already had. Three things follow from the move:

- the message names the caller's argument by construction. From inside the
  shared normalizer, `deparse(substitute(x))` always yielded that helper's own
  formal; it read correctly only because all five verbs spell their first
  formal `.data`, and nothing enforced that.
- `nest_with_margins()` and `nest_by_with_margins()` now admit input the way
  the other verbs do. They reached `assert_nest_possible()` first, so a matrix
  was answered with *must be one of the following classes, which can be
  nested: data.frame, dtplyr\_step* — a `marginplyr_error` naming `.data`, so
  #23's story 26 held, but not the same admission. General admission runs
  first; nesting's narrower constraint still applies to input the shared rule
  admits, which a new arrow expectation pins.
- admission now precedes grouping-spec validation in every verb, where before
  the two ran in a different order in the same verb.

The old test asserted only `class = "marginplyr_error"` for the four
non-summarize entry points, which is why it passed while the nesting verbs
answered differently. It now asserts the message.

**Every error was reported as bad input.** `tryCatch(dplyr::group_vars(x),
error = ...)` treats a backend's own failure — a broken connection, an
upstream defect — as the caller having supplied the wrong kind of object, the
misclassification ADR 0015 warns about from the other direction.
Admissibility is now decided by looking for a registered method: dplyr
registers no `group_vars()` default, so an object no method matches is exactly
the object the generic cannot dispatch on, and a method that exists is never
called here. Verified to admit data frames, tibbles, grouped data frames,
dtplyr, arrow (including `RecordBatchReader`, which `assert_lazy_table()` then
rejects on its own terms) and dbplyr, and to reject matrices, plain lists, and
`NULL`.

**`summary_option_names()` counted `.data` and `...`.** Neither can reach `...`
as a mistaken option name — `.data` matches its own formal exactly, and `...`
is not a name a caller can write — so their only effect was to widen the
near-miss net. `.date = max(date)` was rejected as resembling `.data`, though
it is as ordinary an output name as `.total_by_region`, which this issue's
criterion protects. Both are excluded; `.date` is now an expectation.

**A near miss on a removed option named only what it resembled.**
`.sorts = TRUE` reported *has no `.sort` argument* — a word absent from the
caller's code. Both messages now name what was written. `removed_summary_options`
became a list carrying each entry's own guidance, rather than one
`.sort`-specific sentence parameterized by the matched name, which would have
been confidently wrong for the next entry added.

One finding was left as raised. `check_removed_groups_argument()` (`.groups`)
and `check_option_named_summaries()` are the same shape and run consecutively,
and the registry could now hold `.groups`. Folding it in would newly reject
near misses of `.groups`, which is a behaviour change this issue did not ask
for; it belongs with whichever change next touches that check.

## Misspelling threshold

**Stays at `utils::adist() <= 1`.**

The threshold is asymmetric: narrowing what is rejected after release is safe,
widening it newly rejects names that used to work. So the question is only
whether 1 is already too wide or still too narrow.

Too narrow it is not. Every miss this issue set out to catch is one character
of insertion or deletion — `.sorts`, `.groupings`, `.margin_labels`,
`.duplicate`, `.ids`.

Too wide it is, marginally, and irreducibly. Against the current options the
distance-1 net also catches `.sd`, `.idx`, `.id2`, `.y`, and `.b`, all of them
neighbours of the two 2-character options `.by` and `.id`. `.sd` and `.idx`
are plausible summary names. There is no cheap refinement: charging more for
substitutions (`utils::adist(costs = list(substitutions = 2))`) clears only
`.sd`. `.idx` and `.id2` are insertions, and `.y` and `.b` are deletions from
`.by` — one character added or removed, the same edit shape as `.ids`, which
the criterion above requires be caught. A rule cannot separate them, so the
collision is a property of having 2-character options, not of the number 1.

Widening to 2 is out regardless: `.n` is distance 2 from `.by`, and `.n` is
the most common leading-dot summary name there is and explicitly protected
above.

The error is actionable — it names the option, and renaming the summary
clears it — so the residue is a cost worth carrying. If it is reported in
practice, the fix is to exempt the 2-character options from near-miss matching
and require an exact match for them, which costs only `.ids`.

## Interaction with the planned `.sort` argument

`.sort` is planned for this release as a structural sort (see the roadmap
discussion; it is a different feature from the display-value sort #15
removed). When it ships, `.sort` must be removed from `removed_summary_options`
in `R/summary-selections.R`, and the two `.sort` expectations in
`tests/testthat/test-verb-argument-admission.R` must move to another removed or
misspelled option. **Land this branch first and make that edit part of the
`.sort` PR** — the mechanism is worth having regardless of which options
populate the list.

## Blocks

- #40

body:
Decisions live in
`design/adr/0018-order-margin-results-by-grouping-structure.md`, with
amendments to ADR 0001 and ADR 0009 and the **Margin order** entry in
`CONTEXT.md`. They are not restated here.

## Problem Statement

A caller who produces a multi-grain summary and wants to read it cannot put
it in a sensible order.

Row order is unspecified, so the documented answer is to call
`dplyr::arrange()`. That answer does not work. Sorting by a grouping
dimension's values places a margin row wherever the string `"Total"` falls
among that dimension's values — before `"a"` or after `"z"` depending on the
locale and the label — so subtotals scatter instead of sitting with the rows
they summarize.

The order the caller actually wants keys on whether a dimension was
aggregated, which is a Grouping bit. Callers cannot supply that key
themselves:

- `dplyr::across(c(region, store), grouping_bit)` fails. The summary
  selection proxy excludes every grouping dimension, and independently of
  that, `grouping_bit()` is rewritten syntactically against the Grouping plan
  and accepts only a bare grouping column, never a value handed to it by
  `across()`.
- Writing one `grouping_bit()` summary per dimension by hand, arranging on
  them, and dropping them again loses the order on every dbplyr backend:
  arranging on a column the same query summarized and then dropping it is the
  shape dbplyr flattens, which leaves the `ORDER BY` behind.
- Under `.margin_label = NULL` the order is not expressible at all, because a
  margin and a source missing value are then the same displayed value.

## Solution

`.sort`, a new common option on all four Margin verbs, taking `"none"`,
`"last"`, or `"first"` and defaulting to `"none"`. It produces a **Margin
order**: within each fixed `.by` key, every grouping dimension contributes its
Grouping bit and its missingness before its own value, so a margin row sits
with the rows it summarizes regardless of locale or Margin label.

`.sort` shares only its name with the option removed in #15. That one ordered
by displayed values; this one orders by the Grouping plan's structure.

## User Stories

1. As a report author, I want subtotal rows to appear directly beneath the
   detail rows they summarize, so that I can read a rollup top to bottom
   without cross-referencing.
2. As a report author, I want the grand total row to appear at the end of the
   result, so that the reader finds it where a report puts it.
3. As a report author producing a totals-first layout, I want margin rows to
   precede their detail rows, so that I can publish a summary-first table.
4. As a report author, I want the ordering to be identical whether my data is
   a local data frame, a DuckDB table, or an Arrow dataset, so that changing
   where the data lives does not change what I publish.
5. As a report author whose dimension is an ordered factor, I want rows to
   follow my declared level order rather than alphabetical order, so that
   `small`/`medium`/`large` reads correctly.
6. As a report author, I want missing values to sort last within each Grouping
   bit group on every backend, so that a SQLite result does not start with a
   row that a DuckDB result ends with.
7. As a report author using `.by`, I want each fixed partition to appear as
   one contiguous block, so that partitions do not interleave.
8. As a report author using `.by`, I want the ordering within a partition to be
   independent of every other partition, so that adding a partition does not
   move rows in the others.
9. As a report author, I want `.sort` to work the same way on
   `summarize_with_margins()`, `expand_with_margins()`,
   `nest_with_margins()`, and `nest_by_with_margins()`, so that I do not have
   to learn which verbs support it.
10. As a caller of `nest_by_with_margins()`, I want the row-wise result in
    Margin order, so that iterating over it and recombining yields rows in
    that order.
11. As a caller of `expand_with_margins()`, I want the expanded key skeleton
    ordered, so that I can inspect it directly rather than joining it first.
12. As a caller who does not want ordering, I want row order to remain
    unspecified by default, so that I do not pay for an `ORDER BY` I did not
    request.
13. As a caller on a lazy backend, I want the sorted result to remain lazy, so
    that ordering does not force a collection.
14. As a caller on DuckDB or PostgreSQL, I want ordering not to cost me the
    native `GROUPING SETS` plan, so that asking for a readable result does not
    silently switch me to a slower query.
15. As a caller using `.duplicates = "keep"`, I want `.sort` to be accepted
    without an error and without changing which adapter runs, so that the two
    options compose.
16. As a caller using `.duplicates = "keep"` together with `.id`, I want
    duplicate occurrences to come out adjacent and in Grouping plan order, so
    that the repetition is visible rather than scattered.
17. As a caller using a composite dimension, I want its columns ordered
    together, so that a composite behaves as the single dimension it is.
18. As a caller using `.margin_label = NULL`, I want margins and source
    missing values separated by position even though they display alike, so
    that I can tell them apart without adding `.id`.
19. As a caller who set `.margin_label_position = "first"`, I want row order
    to be unaffected by it, so that the level's position and the row's
    position stay independent decisions.
20. As a caller who writes `.sort = TRUE` from memory of the removed option, I
    want an error naming the three valid choices, so that I reach the right
    spelling in one attempt.
21. As a caller who misspells `.sort` as `.sorts`, I want the near-miss
    diagnostic to name both what I wrote and what I meant, so that I can find
    the word in my own code.
22. As a caller who writes `.groups`, I want a diagnostic that names what
    replaces it, so that the removed option still tells me where to go.
23. As a caller who misspells `.groups`, I want that same guidance rather than
    a generic "captured as a summary" message.
24. As a caller chaining further verbs onto a lazy sorted result, I want the
    documentation to tell me the order may not survive, so that I am not
    surprised when it does not.
25. As a maintainer, I want the ordering contract asserted per backend in the
    release matrix, so that a green job proves the backend actually ordered.

## Implementation Decisions

**`.sort` is a common Margin option.** It joins `.margin_label`,
`.margin_label_position`, `.check_margin_label`, `.duplicates`, and `.id` on
all four verbs, is normalized alongside them in the shared Margin option
normalizer, and is validated with the same choice matcher those options use,
so `.sort = TRUE` produces the standard "must be one of" Package condition.

**The shared finalizer orders rows.** Ordering happens in the Margin
operation finalizer, after it restores factors and places the grouping
columns — restoring first is what makes a factor dimension sort by level, and
ordering last is what keeps the `ORDER BY` outermost. No verb kind is passed
into the shared module: the key comes from the Grouping plan, which the
module already holds. This restores the clause ADR 0001's first amendment
withdrew.

**The sort key.** Per ADR 0018:

```
by1 … byN,  bit(d1), is.na(d1), d1,  bit(d2), is.na(d2), d2,  …,  [set_id]
```

`"first"` reverses the Grouping bits alone. Fixed-key priority and the
Grouping set identifier tiebreak are consequences of the key being the
result's own leading columns in output order, not separate rules.

**Two mechanisms, one rule.** The sort key must be resolvable in the `FROM`
clause of the query carrying the `ORDER BY`.

- A native summary on DuckDB or PostgreSQL orders by an expression over
  `GROUPING(d)` and `d`, which folds into the aggregate query. It adds no
  internal column, so `.sort` never costs the native `GROUPING SETS` plan.
- Every other path — the `UNION ALL` adapter, and `expand_with_margins()` on
  every backend since it always uses that adapter — orders by an expression
  over a per-branch identifier literal. The union is already a subquery, so
  the identifier stays resolvable after the projection drops it.
- The nesting verbs admit only data frames and dtplyr steps and order with an
  ordinary `arrange()`.

Materializing a sort key is not what breaks; the rule above is what must
hold. A prototype ordered on a column the same query summarized and then
dropped it, which dbplyr flattens into the aggregate, leaving an `ORDER BY`
naming a column no longer in `FROM`. DuckDB rejects that with a binder error.

**`.duplicates = "keep"` is unaffected.** Which adapter runs stays a function
of `native_duplicate_sets` alone. No new fallback, no new diagnostic.

**The removed-option mechanism keeps a live entry.** `.sort` leaves the
removed-summary-options list, which would otherwise be empty and its
guidance branch unreachable. `.groups` moves into it and its bespoke check
function is deleted, which also extends near-miss coverage to `.group` and
`.groupss`. Its message becomes:

> `summarize_with_margins()` has no `.groups` argument; Margin-summary
> results are always ungrouped.

## Testing Decisions

A good test here asserts the rows a public verb returns, not how the order was
produced. The ADR deliberately specifies different mechanisms per backend, so
asserting on the internal sort-key builder would freeze one of them.

**S1 — the public verbs, one new file `tests/testthat/test-margin-order.R`.**
Mirrors `test-margin-id.R`, the prior art for a common Margin option: one
file covering all four verbs, the duplicate policy, both adapters, and
laziness. Every row-order assertion goes through a public verb and compares
returned rows with `expect_identical()`. This seam carries the key
definition, `"first"` inverting bits alone, factor level order, missing-last,
`.by` contiguity, the Grouping set identifier tiebreak, composite dimensions,
`.duplicates = "keep"`, `.margin_label_position` independence, the `"none"`
default, and the vocabulary error.

**S2 — rendered SQL.** `dbplyr::sql_render()` against a simulated
connection, as `test-margin-id.R` already does for `.id`. Carries only what
rows cannot show: that a native summary keeps `GROUP BY GROUPING SETS`, emits
its `ORDER BY` over `GROUPING(...)`, and adds no internal column; and that the
union path keeps its branch identifier resolvable. No database, deterministic.

**S3 — executed order on real backends.** `skip_if_backend_absent()` with a
real connection, as `test-margin-id.R` does for the DuckDB `.id` agreement.
Carries what a rendered query cannot prove: that the backend returns the rows
in that order, that native and portable adapters agree, and that DuckDB,
SQLite, dtplyr, and Arrow agree with local results.

**Existing seams edited, not added.** The verb-formals symmetry test moves
`.sort` from its negative assertion to a positive one in the shape the
`.check_margin_label` and `.margin_label_position` assertions already use;
the verb-argument-admission tests move their two `.sort` expectations to
`.groups`; one message snapshot updates.

**No row-order snapshots.** testthat skips snapshots under CRAN semantics, so
a row-order snapshot would prove nothing in most jobs, and row order is
exactly assertable. The `.groups` message stays a snapshot, which is what
that seam is for.

**Release matrix.** Each backend job's `proves` list must name the new
contract tests it exists to execute. `verify-backend.R` fails a job when a
named test did not run, but does not fail when a test exists and is not
named — so a contract test added without a `proves` entry passes CI while
proving nothing about that backend.

## Out of Scope

- **`.bits`**, an argument exposing Grouping bit columns for the caller to
  arrange on. Rejected in ADR 0018 on measurement.
- **Making the sort key configurable.** `.sort` selects a direction for
  margins; it does not take columns, and there is no plan to add that.
- **Promising that the order survives further verbs on a lazy backend.**
  Explicitly not promised. No wrapper, no warning, no re-application.
- **Unblocking `across(c(region, store), grouping_bit)`.** The proxy
  exclusion and the bare-symbol requirement are separate existing decisions
  and neither changes here.
- **Ordering `inspect_grouping()`.** It already guarantees Grouping-plan
  order under ADR 0013, which is a different order and unaffected.
- **Any change to `.id` semantics.** `.id` is neither required by `.sort` nor
  implied by it.

## Further Notes

`.sort` was previously rejected outright by the removed-option check added in
#77, which is merged. Removing that entry is part of this work, not a
prerequisite.

Documentation to update beyond the help pages: `design/architecture.md`
states that finalization leaves row ordering unspecified, which becomes true
only by default, and that file links every other ADR, so it needs a link to
ADR 0018. `NEWS.md` needs an entry. The `@param` text must say what the key
is, since the argument name does not reveal it.

CRAN has not seen 0.1.0, so there is no compatibility constraint — but the
vocabulary and the scope of the promise are fixed at release, which is why
ADR 0018 records both.
